quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: This guide uses O*NET's Data Warehousing Specialists profile, the closest O*NET occupation: they design, model or implement corporate data warehousing, program and configure warehouses of database information, and support the people who use them.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Data Warehousing Specialists) include Data Warehouse Analyst and Data Warehouse Solution Architect.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a data engineer does
paragraphs: This guide uses O*NET's Data Warehousing Specialists profile, the closest O*NET occupation: they design, model or implement corporate data warehousing, program and configure warehouses of database information, and support the people who use them.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Data Warehousing Specialists. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Develop the processes that source, load, transform and extract data.
Map data between source systems, data warehouses and data marts.
Design and build warehouse database structures.
Verify the structure, accuracy and quality of warehouse data.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering; MCA (Master of Computer Applications); Software Developer.
Less common routes on the map: BCA (Bachelor of Computer Applications); Business Intelligence Analyst.
